name: Élisabeth Baume-Schneider
role: Federal Councillor, Head of the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA)
bio: Élisabeth Baume-Schneider (born 21 December 1963 in Saint-Imier, originally from Les Breuleux, raised in Les Bois, canton of Jura) is a Swiss Social Democratic politician and member of the Federal Council. She is the first person from the canton of Jura ever elected to the Federal Council, chosen by the United Federal Assembly on 7 December 2022 to succeed Simonetta Sommaruga, defeating party favourite Eva Herzog in the third round (123 votes to 116). Trained as a social worker, she earned a licentiate in economic and social sciences from the University of Neuchâtel (1987) and worked in social and medico-social services in the Franches-Montagnes and the canton of Jura until 2001, later directing the School of Social Work and Health (HETSL) in Lausanne. She served in the Jura cantonal parliament (1995–2002, president 2000) and in the Jura cantonal government (2002–2015), heading the Department of Education, Culture and Sport. She represented Jura in the Council of States from 2019 to 2022. In the Federal Council she headed the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP/DFJP) during 2023, then took over the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA/DFI) on 1 January 2024.
